ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP and sanctions screening is required for all directors, general partners, limited partners holding 10% or more of economic interests, and authorised signatories. Screening databases include the UN Consolidated List, UK HM Treasury Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, Bermuda Sanctions List, and the FATF Watchlist. Enhanced due diligence applies to any PEP, including verification of source of funds and heightened transaction monitoring for at least 3 months. Automated screening is conducted at onboarding, upon any new sanctions designation, and at least quarterly thereafter.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Bermuda Companies Registry – Name Reservation and Clearance portal (Registrar of Companies, Government of Bermuda)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the mandatory statutory language for corporate names. The proposed name must be in Latin-script characters and, for an exempted limited partnership, must end with 'L.P.' or otherwise identify the partnership as limited. Non-English names require a certified English transliteration and translation. Chinese characters, Cyrillic script, or any non-Latin alphabet are not accepted in the registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a written appeal within 14 days of rejection notice under section 13 of the Companies Act 1981 (applied mutatis mutandis to exempted partnerships). The appeal must state the grounds of objection and may propose two alternative names. The Registrar must issue a determination within 30 days. If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may file a fresh name reservation immediately after 7 days, or seek judicial review in the Supreme Court of Bermuda.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted for the licensed customs brokerage ELP. A physical street address in Bermuda is required for the registered office and for the customs brokerage licence. A virtual office may be used for ancillary correspondence only, but not for the statutory registered office or the licensed activity; the Bermuda Customs Department requires a physical business premises for the licensed customs brokerage.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 45% (higher than an ordinary ELP because the customs brokerage licence triggers Bermuda Customs Department on-site inspections under the Customs Tariff Act 1971, and the Bermuda Monetary Authority may conduct AML/CFT business inspections).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Exempted Limited Partnership Act 2015 (Bermuda), ss. 4 (application for registration), 5 (certificate of registration), 6 (name), 7 (registered office), 8 (general partner) and 9 (limited partners).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Corporate Registry, Government of Bermuda, Hamilton
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form ELP 1 - Application for Registration of an Exempted Limited Partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. Contributions are fixed by the limited partnership agreement and may be cash, property or promissory notes. No escrow account or deposit is required at formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) the General Partner adopts the Exempted Limited Partnership Agreement and ratifies the capital subscription commitments of each limited partner as reflected in the capital ledger; (2) the registered office of the Partnership shall be located at [address], Hamilton, Bermuda, and [name] is appointed authorized representative and compliance officer and [name] is appointed principal administrative officer, each being authorized to file the registration application, execute customs brokerage licence applications, and open the operating account; (4) the authorized signatory of the General Partner is authorized to submit all statutory filings, declarations, and ancillary agreements. All preliminary actions taken by the promoters are hereby ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Corporate Registry, Government of Bermuda
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for name approval through the Bermuda Registry portal or paper form. The proposed name must contain 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' and must not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered entity. Include the general partner's details and written consent. On approval, the name is reserved for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Written consent of the proposed general partner
Certificate of incorporation and register of directors of the corporate general partner, if any
Photographic identification of the general partner and ultimate beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity, amended alternative names may be submitted in writing and the reservation file transferred without an additional application fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Exempted Limited Partnership Registration Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Corporate Registry, Government of Bermuda
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and execute Form ELP 1. State the registered office address in Bermuda, identify all general and limited partners, set out capital contribution amounts, and attach a certified copy of the exempted limited partnership agreement. The declaration of the general partner must be signed before a notary public or commissioner of oaths. Pay the prescribed registration fee and submit the completed file to the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Completed Form ELP 1
Declaration of the general partner
Exempted Limited Partnership Agreement
Consent to act of the Bermuda registered office provider
Schedule of general and limited partners with capital contributions
AML/KYC documentation for all partners and controllers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues an information query, respond within 14 calendar days with the requested clarification. If registration is refused, correct the stated defect and refile, or appeal to the Supreme Court of Bermuda within the applicable limitation period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate Issuance and Registered Office Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies and the appointed Bermuda registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Registration. Confirm the registered office with the licensed agent, appoint the resident authorised representative, and maintain the register of limited partners at the registered office. Add the company details to internal governance books and issue partnership interests or documentation to the partners.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration issued by the Registrar
Written consent of the Bermuda registered agent
Appointment form for resident authorised representative
Register of limited partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a clerical error, submit a correction request to the Registrar. If the registered agent withdraws consent, designate another licensed agent and file the new consent immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Customs Brokerage Licence and Regulatory Authorisation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Customs Department - Licensing Section; HM Revenue & Customs Customs Intermediary Team for UK declaration handling
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a customs broker licence application together with the ELP registration certificate, evidence of a fixed place of business, professional indemnity cover, identity of responsible officers, and an AML/CFT manual reflecting medium-risk enhanced customer due diligence. If the partnership will act as a UK customs representative, apply for the HMRC customs intermediary authorisation and register for the Customs Declaration Service.
required_dossiers: Customs broker licence application form
Certificate of ELP registration
AML/CFT policy and customer due diligence procedures
Fit-and-proper declarations for responsible officers and partners
Professional indemnity insurance certificate
Proof of operational premises in Bermuda
HMRC customs intermediary authorisation application, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licensing authority raises a deficiency, submit the supplemental information within the stated response period. If the licence is refused, request written reasons and appeal to the Bermuda Customs Appeal Tribunal or HMRC First-tier Tribunal within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Department of Environment and Natural Resources; Department of Planning; Bermuda Fire and Rescue Service; Department of Labour
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For an office-based brokerage operation, no full environmental impact report is required; prepare a preliminary environmental screening checklist and obtain development permit or change-of-use approval for any physical alterations. For bonded transit or storage premises, submit a building design with structural load certification, fire-safety layout, spill-containment measures, and obtain a certificate of occupancy before operations commence.
required_dossiers: Development permit or change-of-use application
Preliminary environmental screening checklist
Fire safety compliance certificate
Structural load certification for bonded goods storage areas
Occupational health and safety clearance
Stormwater and drainage connection approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If environmental or building conditions are imposed, submit a compliance schedule and revised drawings to the relevant authority. A stop-work order may be appealed to the Planning Appeals Board or similar tribunal within 21 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Bermuda Customs Department - Licensing Section; HM Revenue & Customs Customs Intermediary Team
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Customs Broker Licence (Bermuda) and, where applicable, HMRC Customs Representative Authorisation (UK)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Bermuda Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II - Registration / Preliminary Environmental Screening; full EIA only if bonded transit storage, industrial activity or substantial land disturbance is proposed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process discharge is authorised for a customs brokerage office. Domestic wastewater must connect to the public sewer or a licensed septic system. Stormwater drainage must not contact stored goods or waste materials. Any combustion plant must meet applicable Bermudian clean air standards; VOC-emitting substances must be stored in closed containers and total site VOC emissions shall not exceed 0.5 kg/day.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Statement from the Bermuda Fire and Rescue Service; structural load inspection and Certificate of Occupancy from the Department of Planning for any bonded storage premises; and occupational health and safety clearance from the Bermuda Department of Labour under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 1982.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Bermuda Customs Department and the Office of the Tax Commissioner (OTAX), Bermuda Ministry of Finance; digital portals: https://www.gov.bm/customs (ASYCUDA World single window) and https://www.otax.bm
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the ELP with the Bermuda Registrar of Companies under the Exempted Limited Partnership Act 2015 to obtain the ELP registration number. Step 2: File the annual Declaration of Exempted Partnership renewal and obtain a Certificate of Compliance / Tax Residence Certificate from the Ministry of Finance for TIEA and foreign-tax relief. Step 3: Apply to Bermuda Customs for a Customs Brokers' Licence under section 8 of the Customs Act 1965, evidencing a registered business address, fit-and-proper personnel, a surety bond, and the intended Customs Processing Code. Step 4: Enrol in ASYCUDA World to receive a declarant/agent ID for electronic clearance. Foreign entities without a Bermuda branch may engage a locally licensed counterparty; a physical place of business or agent is operationally required for a broker licence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. Bermuda levies no corporate income tax, capital gains tax, or VAT. The ELP is statutorily a transparent partnership under the Exempted Limited Partnership Act 2015; under US check-the-box and UK transparent-entity rules it is treated as pass-through unless an affirmative Form 8832 election to be taxed as an association is filed. Economic substance obligations under the Economic Substance Act 2018 apply only to relevant activities, and customs brokerage is not a relevant activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under the Exempted Limited Partnership Act 2015, the ELP may elect in its exempted partnership declaration to be a limited-liability partnership; no local election for income-tax treatment exists because Bermuda has no income tax. For foreign purposes, an IRS Form 8832 check-the-box election may be made to treat the ELP as either transparent or an association taxable as a corporation, including hybrid-mismatch positioning; UK hybrid mismatch rules (Taxation (International and Other Provisions) Act 2010) require matching adjustments only where the ELP derives UK-source income. The ELP may also file a non-relevant entity return under the Economic Substance Regulations to evidence that no economic substance obligations attach.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Bermuda has no VAT, GST, or sales and use tax. The sole indirect levy is the Customs Duties Act 1974: import duties at 0-25% ad valorem plus specific duties on alcohol, tobacco, and fuel. Customs clearance and brokerage services are outside the charge to duty; broker fees carry no output VAT, and the only tax leakage is statutory import duty on physical goods and the annual customs broker licence fee.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable - no VAT/GST regime, so no economic turnover threshold activates an indirect-tax registration. However, any person carrying on business as a customs broker must hold a Customs Brokers' Licence under section 8 of the Customs Act 1965, supported by a surety bond in a penal sum set by the Collector of Customs (commonly BMD 25,000 or higher depending on projected annual clearance volume). There is no SME exemption from the licence requirement.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Bermuda Customs operates the ASYCUDA World single window; all import, export, and transit entries are filed electronically in real time via API/XML or the web interface using the declarant's ASYCUDA ID. There is no fiscal e-invoicing or digital stamping mandate for broker invoices because no invoice-based indirect tax exists; however, the ASYCUDA entry is digitally stamped by Customs and generates a Customs Release Reference required before any physical release of goods. Bonded transit movements require electronic frontier declarations in ASYCUDA plus periodic reconciliation reports.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Bermuda, or entered for transit or transshipment under a customs suspension procedure, are not chargeable with import duty and are effectively zero-rated: the exporter or forwarding broker must file an outward cargo declaration (Form CUS-10 / ASYCUDA outward entry), identify the destination country, and record the vessel, vehicle, or flight details within the statutory period. Services rendered by a customs broker to overseas principals are outside Bermuda's tax net because no Bermuda output tax exists, so no service-related VAT refund mechanism is required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bermuda Customs Outward Export Declaration (Form CUS-10 / ASYCUDA electronic outward entry)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from Bermuda
Certificate of Origin (where preferential origin treatment is claimed)
Commercial invoice and packing list bearing the ELP broker's unique reference
Customs Broker's Licence number and ASYCUDA declarant code
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice evidencing receipt of commission proceeds from foreign principals
Bonded transit movement record / customs-goods register for transit and transshipment cargo
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under the Customs Act 1965 and the Customs Duties Act 1974, erroneous zero-rating or false export entries attract retrospective demand of unpaid duty, a civil penalty of up to three times the duty evaded or BMD 5,000 (whichever is greater), forfeiture of the goods, and suspension or revocation of the Customs Brokers' Licence. Knowingly making a false statement in an ASYCUDA export declaration is an indictable offence punishable by imprisonment of up to 3 years and a fine of up to BMD 20,000, with the broker jointly and severally liable with the importer or exporter. Because the ELP operates a Medium_Risk_Enhanced licensed cash-heavy trade, intensified AML-integrity scrutiny and Customs audit reviews apply with retrospective clawback exposure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Bermudian dollar (BMD) is pegged at parity to the United States dollar (USD), and USD is accepted as legal tender in circulation throughout Bermuda. Bermuda operates a fully liberalised capital and current account for exempted entities: the Exchange Control Act 1972 and subordinate Exchange Control Regulations are administered by the BMA, but exempted undertakings such as the KY_ELP qualify for a general Exchange Control permit that removes all restrictions on inward capital, dividend and interest repatriation, profit remittance, and liquidation proceeds. There are no statutory profit-remittance hurdles, no prior-approval queue, and no minimum holding period for foreign-currency proceeds. Non-resident partners may receive distributions and capital withdrawals in the currency of choice (BMD, USD, GBP, or EUR) through correspondent clearing without further BMA reference. The only residual controls are the maintenance of a designated account at a BMA-licensed bank and the filing of suspicious-transaction reports under the Proceeds of Crime (Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing) Regulations 2018.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable in Bermuda. There is no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export-proceeds surrender; Bermuda abolished surrender obligations for non-resident and exempted accounts in 1973 and fully liberalised external payments thereafter. The KY_ELP, as an exempted limited partnership, is categorised as non-resident for Exchange Control purposes and may retain 100% of brokerage commissions and bonded-transit management fees in the original currency (USD, GBP, or EUR) indefinitely. The only compliance duty is to book all export-related receipts accurately and to present a valid Exchange Control permit or reliance letter from the licensed corporate service provider when customs brokerage fees on bonded transit are routed through the Bermudian banking system.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency account (BMD/USD/GBP/EUR) with sub-ledger for customs-fee clearing and trust-account segregation
Operational account with trade-services module (Commercial Letters of Credit, Import/Export Guarantees, SWIFT MT103 clearing)
Capital escrow account and segregated beneficiary-interest trust account for bonded-transit consignments

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as the primary clearing spine; Medium as a secondary disbursement rail. Bermuda has no dedicated e-money institution (EMI) licensing regime distinct from deposit-taking, and a full banking licence is required to hold client funds. UK FCA-authorised EMIs (e.g. Revolut Business, Wise, Currencycloud, Modulr) and EU PSD2 EMIs are legally usable as ancillary top-up or pay-out rails because Bermuda law does not restrict the ELP from holding receivables in an overseas account; however, they cannot replace a BMA-licensed bank for onward third-party settlement into the customs-clearing chain. Material constraints: (i) EMIs are not BMA-designated institutions, so payment routing to HM Revenue & Customs and Bermuda Customs must ultimately land on a licensed correspondent bank; (ii) source-of-funds evidence for USD flows through EMIs frequently triggers enhanced scrutiny at the receiving Bermudian bank, delaying liquidity; and (iii) the medium-enhanced AML risk tier for licensed customs brokers requires any overseas EMI to be named as a sub-agent in client-money arrangements and contractually bound to the Bermuda AML/ATF framework.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permitted only case-by-case under BMA AML/ATF guidance with enhanced due diligence (EDD). There is no absolute statutory mandate for all directors to appear physically, but the ELP's registered agent and the signatories to the account mandate must hold a live BMA-subject relationship with the chosen bank. In practice, Butterfield and HSBC Bermuda require the general partner's authorised signatory to complete at least one in-person or notarised video-interview verification, supported by a Bermuda-registered office address and an appointed local AML compliance officer. If the ELP has a corporate general partner with no natural-person directors physically present in Bermuda, the bank will demand: (i) an original notarised resolution confirming ultimate signatories; (ii) a certificate of incumbency from the Bermudian secretary; and (iii) a pre-onboarding interview with a named principal at the bank's Hamilton office or via certified online identity-verification technology meeting BMA and Association of Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialists (ACAMS) benchmarks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity of the exempted limited partnership structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full chain-of-title schedule from the UK parent entity down to each KY_ELP limited partner; Bermuda Beneficial Ownership register filing certificate; registered agent reliance letter under the Corporate Service Provider (CSP) Business Act 2020; legal opinion from a Bermuda law firm confirming the 25% threshold analysis and the absence of bearer interests.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory licence validation for customs brokerage services
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bermuda Customs Department broker licence or customs code certificate; HM Revenue & Customs Customs Broker registration; ISIC 5229 activity description corroborated by services agreement; regulatory-licence sample and website; confirmation that the brokerage house is not acting as an unlicensed freight forwarder under the Bermuda Airports and Ports Acts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border transactions with UK and EU counterparties generating sanctions and PEP screening alerts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Adverse-media investigation report; sanctions-screening result from a reputable vendor evidencing low-match resolution; PEP source-of-wealth declaration for any UK or EU partner; contract file of underlying shipments with customs entry numbers; corporate structure chart and liability warranties of the general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds ambiguity arising from receivables on bonded transit and customs-fee collections
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or management financial statements for the last two years; customs-computed duty assessment documentation; invoicing ledger, export-import manifests, and carrier bills of lading; bank reference letter from the UK parent's existing lender; sworn certificate of the general partner confirming that collected customs taxes and duties are held in trust and never commingled with fees.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction nexus of end-beneficiary cargo owners in sanctioned or grey-listed jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FATF and EU Consolidated List compliance matrix; documentary evidence of the ultimate consignee's export-compliance licence; transaction-level embargo screening certificates; independent third-party cargo verification report; enforceable representation-and-warranty clause requiring the counterparty to bear liability for misrepresentation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires a board-authorised capital-contribution wire from the UK parent to the KY_ELP's BMA-licensed bank account in GBP or USD, transmitted by SWIFT MT103 with the remitter referencing the ELP's legal name and registered number. Use purpose code 'C.03 – Capital contributions to partnerships' or the equivalent BOP code generated by the remitting UK bank, with the reference 'EQUITY INJECTION – ELP PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT ART. X'. The receiving Bermudian bank verifies the sender's AML declaration and the beneficiary account mandate. For amounts exceeding USD 50,000, the corporate service provider must obtain the unaudited capital ledger, the general partner's capital-call notice, and a short legal opinion confirming that the injection is not a loan requiring Exchange Control approval, thereby allowing full reserving without BMA reference.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements are executed over SWIFT MT103 direct-clearing for brokerage fee payments and customs-duty transfers to HM Revenue & Customs and Bermuda Customs. For high-value bonded-transit shipments involving title retention, a Commercial Letter of Credit issued by HSBC Bermuda or Butterfield and confirmed by a UK correspondent bank provides the settlement spine. Clearing rails: (i) USD balances clear intraday via the New York correspondent (Fedwire/CHIPS) through the Bermudian bank's US respondent; (ii) GBP balances settle over CHAPS; (iii) EUR disbursements clear over TARGET2 using a settlement account at a UK clearing bank; and (iv) the Automated_Broker_Interface_ACH rail is used only for monthly net-settlement of customs-duty batches with HMRC, not for beneficiary-specific commercial payments. All outbound disbursements must carry purpose code 'S.02 – Payment for services' or 'D.03 – Taxes and duties remittance', with the attachment including the underlying customs declaration number, invoice, and the correspondent bank's Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference (UETR) for tracing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot USD/BMD conversion at the 1:1 peg within BMA-licensed banks (no booking requirement)
Outright forward foreign-exchange contracts (USD/GBP and USD/EUR) executed with a BMA Class E licensed bank or an internationally rated counterparty under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on exotic settlement currencies cited in bonded-transit invoices where delivery in the quoted currency is restricted by the counterparty's home state
Cross-currency swap agreements (USD/GBP and USD/EUR) for multi-year payment commitments entered as cash-flow hedges under the partnership's treasury policy
European-style FX options purchased on a zero-premium collar basis to floor seasonal GBP payroll and HMRC duty-remittance costs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Exempted Partnership Annual Return and Annual Government Fee Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January immediately following the end of the previous calendar year; no extension is available for exempted partnerships
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of BMD 500 plus a 10% surcharge on the unpaid annual fee; continued default beyond three months exposes the partnership to administrative strike-off and a formal restoration application with reinstatement fees

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and Continuation Statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda, through the Bermuda-resident registered agent and the Beneficial Ownership Secure Search system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual reaffirmation due by 31 January for the preceding calendar year; any individual change in limited partners or beneficial ownership must additionally be filed within 21 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of up to BMD 10,000 plus daily compounding penalties for unrectified inaccuracies; persistent non-compliance may lead to suspension of the registered agent's submission rights and flagging of the partnership as non-compliant

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance Annual Return (Form ES) Only if a Relevant Activity Is Undertaken; a Purely Domestic Customs Brokerage Ordinarily Reports No Relevant Activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda, Economic Substance Compliance Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the financial period; where no relevant activity is carried on, no separate economic substance return is required for a purely local customs brokerage house
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission penalty of BMD 3,000 with further compliance intervention; material economic substance deficiencies can trigger de-registration and disqualification of the general partner

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No universal statutory audit is imposed on an Exempted Limited Partnership under Bermuda's Exempted Limited Partnership Act 2015. A mandatory independent audit crystallises where: (i) the partnership agreement, a financier covenant, or a sectoral licence condition requires certified accounts; (ii) the partnership belongs to a multinational group with consolidated revenue of EUR 750 million or more and therefore falls within the Economic Transition (Corporate Income Tax) Act 2023; or (iii) the Registrar or Minister exercises the discretion to call for audited financial statements
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Bermuda does not maintain a locally codified general-purpose GAAP; IFRS is the customary and accepted accounting framework for exempted partnerships, with US GAAP permissible where the ultimate parent reporting framework so requires

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Bermuda-resident registered agent audits and reaffirms the Beneficial Ownership Register each calendar year; all transfers of partnership interests and changes to beneficial ownership are reported to the Registrar within 21 days of the change, and the annual consolidated confirmation is submitted by 31 January, re-attributing all year-end interests to the correct beneficial owners
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Partnership Consents and Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - 3,200 per annum for the Bermuda registered office plus resident registered agent and compliance services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,500 - 22,000 per annum for a full IFRS partnership audit by a first-tier or mid-tier Bermuda firm; a review engagement generally ranges from USD 4,000 - 8,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for standard Exempted Limited Partnerships; 15% for in-scope Multinational Enterprise Groups under the Corporate Income Tax Act 2023 (CITA) for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2025
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: None; Bermuda imposes no corporate income tax, capital gains tax, or preferential tax holidays on exempted partnerships. No investment allowances, enhanced deductions, or patent box regimes exist under domestic law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No Bermuda corporate income tax return is required for an Exempted Limited Partnership outside the scope of CITA 2023. Annual compliance is satisfied via the Registrar of Companies e-services portal (www.rec.gov.bm) filing under the Exempted Partnerships Act 2015.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 60 days of the anniversary of the partnership's registration, or by the date stated in the certificate of compliance; no tax extension is available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name of the exempted partnership exactly as registered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the name from the certificate of formation; no translation or acronym variation is permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical Bermuda street address of the registered office maintained by the local service provider.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A P.O. Box is insufficient; provide the full address including parish and postal code.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, jurisdiction of incorporation, and registered number of each general partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the general partner is a non-Bermudian entity, attach a certificate of good standing from its home registry.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification that the partnership has not contravened the Exempted Partnerships Act and that all fees are paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be signed by the Bermuda resident representative or general partner; a false declaration constitutes an offence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: BD$500 per month or part thereof, up to BD$12,000; the Registrar may strike the partnership off the register; general partners may be disqualified from acting in Bermuda for up to 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form CIT-2) and associated schedules under the Corporate Income Tax Act 2023; filed through the Bermuda Office of the Tax Commissioner e-filing portal (taxauth.bm).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with quarterly instalment payments for in-scope MNE groups
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 15 months after the end of the fiscal year of the ultimate parent entity; for the first CITA period (FY starting 1 January 2025), the return is due no later than 30 April 2026, as gazetted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part 1 – Group and Constituent Entity Identification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the ultimate parent, its jurisdiction, and all constituent entities, including the ELP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply only if the ELP belongs to an MNE group with consolidated revenue of at least €750M; state the global legal entity identifier if available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the ELP's financial accounting profit or loss adjusted under CITA and the OECD GloBE model rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the currency of the group's consolidated accounts; attach a reconciliation between local statutory accounts and covered profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part 3 – Effective Tax Rate and Top-Up Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of the jurisdiction effective tax rate and any top-up tax owed to Bermuda or an equivalent regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Because an ELP is pass-through, first determine whether the partnership is a taxable constituent entity or a transparent entity; if transparent, partners are separately assessed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file: fixed penalty BD$500 plus BD$100 per day of default; incorrect return penalty up to 10% of the additional top-up tax assessed; interest at the prevailing commercial rate plus 4% on unpaid tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Bermuda imposes no withholding tax on distributions, dividends, or partnership allocations. Consequently, no domestic treaty relief protocol exists. Partners seeking foreign tax credits may apply for a Certificate of Tax Residence from the Office of the Tax Commissioner using Form TCR-01, but such a certificate merely evidences residence for CITA purposes. Bermuda has no comprehensive double taxation agreements, and the UK–Bermuda relationship is governed by a Tax Information Exchange Agreement; treaty benefits are not available for outbound dividends. Non-resident partners must rely on unilateral foreign tax credits in their own jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory withholding; no treaty rate is applicable because Bermuda has no income tax treaties. Payments of IP royalties, debt interest, and management fees leave Bermuda free of withholding tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No Bermuda transfer-pricing threshold for standalone entities. For an ELP in an in-scope MNE group, mandatory OECD Pillar Two documentation applies when consolidated group revenue exceeds €750M (approximately BD$750M, with conversion determined under the CITA regulations). No local Master File or Local File is required outside the CITA context.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance Act 2018 applies to every 'relevant entity' conducting a 'relevant activity' in Bermuda. Customs brokerage services, if performed by an exempted partnership with a Bermuda licence, constitute a 'relevant activity' of a service business. The partnership must demonstrate: (i) physical premises in Bermuda; (ii) adequate qualified employees; (iii) substantial operating expenditure; and (iv) senior management present in Bermuda. The ELP may claim exemption if it is tax resident in a foreign jurisdiction and provides certified evidence; otherwise, a strict economic substance test must be satisfied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally or recklessly submitting false or misleading information to the Bermuda Office of the Tax Commissioner, concealing group revenues to avoid CITA registration, or manipulating covered profits to reduce top-up tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under CITA 2023, a fine of up to BD$50,000 and a penalty equal to 100% of the top-up tax underpaid; interest on the default from the due date; the tax authority may impose a public disclosure order.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners and any officers who directed, consented to, or negligently permitted the default are jointly and severally liable for the penalty. Criminal conviction may lead to imprisonment for up to 7 years and a disqualification order barring management of any Bermudian entity for 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the ELP as a shell with no substantive commercial activity in Bermuda while falsely claiming non-resident tax status to escape the Economic Substance requirements, or failing to file the economic substance declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Economic Substance Act 2018, a penalty of BD$10,000, plus BD$100 per day for continuing non-compliance. Subsequent offences carry a fine of BD$56,000 and potential striking-off; the Registrar may apply to the Supreme Court for a winding-up order.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners and local representatives may be subjected to restoration costs and disqualification. The Registrar is empowered to publish the names of non-compliant entities, damaging the individuals' standing; persistent evasion may support a criminal prosecution with imprisonment up to 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Violations and Trade-Based Money Laundering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to adopt and maintain an anti-money laundering compliance programme, neglecting customer due diligence, failing to report suspicious transactions, or knowingly facilitating customs fraud, under-invoicing, trade-based money laundering, or sanctions evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing) Regulations 2018, fines up to BD$2 million and imprisonment up to 7 years for money laundering. The Customs Brokerage Licence may be revoked, and the assets of the partnership can be seized.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, general partners, and compliance officers are individually prosecutable. The Supreme Court may impose travel bans, asset freezing orders, confiscation orders, and debarment from holding a role in any regulated financial or customs business for a period not exceeding 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Customs Brokerage and Duty Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a customs broker without a valid Bermuda licence, knowingly under-declaring dutiable goods, mis-describing commodities, or facilitating smuggling through the transshipment or bonded transit process.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Customs Tariff Act and the Bermuda Customs Management Act, fines up to BD$40,000 per violation, forfeiture of goods and vessels, revocation of the brokerage licence, and suspension from the Automated Broker Interface for up to 3 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals engaged in smuggling face fines and imprisonment up to 10 years. Directors or partners who direct such activities are jointly liable for customs duties evaded and may be subject to civil restitution, travel prohibitions while assets are located, and permanent disqualification from customs brokerage licensing.
